ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a parabola (with a fixed shape) intersects the x-axis at points E and F (point E is to the left of point F), and its vertex P moves along the segment $AB$. If the coordinates of points A and B are respectively $(-2, -3)$ and $(4, -3)$, and the minimum value of the x-coordinate of point E is $-5$, what is the maximum value of the x-coordinate of point F?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the axis of symmetry be the line $x=a$, and E, F are symmetric about $x=a$,\\
then $a-x_{E}=x_{F}-a$, $2a=x_{F}+x_{E}$,\\
since the shape of the parabola is fixed,\\
thus, the opening size of the parabola remains unchanged,\\
by translation, it is known that, when P is at point A, the x-coordinate of E is the minimum,\\
when P is at point A, we have $2 \times (-2) = -5 + x_{F}$, solving gives $x_{F}=1$,\\
thus $x_{F}-x_{E}$ is a constant value $1-(-5)=6$,\\
when P moves to B, the maximum of $x_{F}$ is $4+\frac{6}{2}=\boxed{7}$,

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, a parabola (with a fixed shape) intersects the x-axis at points E and F (point E is to the left of point F), and its vertex P moves along the segment AB. If the coordinates of points A and B are respectively (-2, -3) and (4, -3), and the minimum value of the x-coordinate of point E is -5, what is the maximum value of the x-coordinate of point F?
raw_record.answer: Solution: Let the axis of symmetry be the line x = a, and E, F are symmetric about x = a, then a - x_E = x_F - a, so 2a = x_F + x_E. Since the shape of the parabola is fixed, its opening remains unchanged. By translation, when P is at point A, the x-coordinate of E is minimum. When P is at A: 2 × (-2) = -5 + x_F, so x_F = 1. Thus x_F - x_E is constant: 1 - (-5) = 6. When P moves to B, the maximum x_F is 4 + 6/2 = 7.

The maximum x_F is obtained when the vertex is farthest to the right, that is, P is at point B, at this time a=4, therefore x_F=4+6/2=7.
